draft: NEW DRAFT 3.0-draft5l by Board Master, rebuilt from standard shop practice after the 2026-10-13 data loss. NOT 2.5.3.2. Values marked shopDefault:true are my defaults, not recovered values.
description: End-grain slices offset by half a block for a brick or basketweave pattern.

steps.title: Mill rough stock
steps.description: Joint one face and one edge on the jointer, then plane to final thickness plus 1/8" (3 mm). Rest overnight, then plane to final thickness. Take ~1/64" (0.4 mm) passes for the last two passes.
safetyBanners: WARNING: Use push blocks on the jointer. Never joint stock shorter than 12" (305 mm) or thinner than 1/2" (12.7 mm).
WARNING: Keep hands clear of the infeed and outfeed. Feed only boards at least 12" (305 mm) long.

steps.title: Rip strips
steps.description: Rip strips with the jointed edge against the fence. Measure from the fence face to the near side of a tooth set toward the fence.
safetyBanners: WARNING: Use the riving knife and blade guard on every through cut.
WARNING: Use a push stick for any rip narrower than 6" (152 mm). Never reach over or behind the blade.

steps.title: Glue up
steps.description: Glue the first edge-grain panel. Alternate clamps above and below the panel and check for flat with a straightedge.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use a waterproof PVA glue rated for indirect food contact. Clamp until squeeze-out turns rubbery, then scrape.

steps.title: Flatten first panel
steps.description: Plane or sand the panel flat. It is still long grain, so the planer is allowed here if the panel is no wider than 12" (305 mm); a wider panel goes to the router sled or drum sander.
safetyBanners: WARNING: Keep hands clear of the infeed and outfeed. Feed only boards at least 12" (305 mm) long.

steps.title: Crosscut slices
steps.description: Crosscut the panel into slices of the final board thickness plus the end-grain flattening allowance (5 mm), on a crosscut sled with a stop block.

settings.Slice length: final board thickness from cut list

safetyBanners: DANGER: Never use the rip fence as a length stop for crosscuts. Use a crosscut sled with a stop block set before the blade, so the offcut is never trapped between blade and fence.
WARNING: Do not cut pieces shorter than 6" (152 mm) free-hand on the table saw. Use a sled with a hold-down.

steps.title: Rotate slices
steps.description: Turn each slice end grain up.

steps.title: Offset slices
steps.description: Shift every other slice by half a block. Trim the ragged ends after glue-up.

steps.title: Glue up
steps.description: Glue slices with the offset held by a spacer. Alternate clamps above and below the panel and check for flat with a straightedge.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use a waterproof PVA glue rated for indirect food contact. Clamp until squeeze-out turns rubbery, then scrape.

steps.title: Trim ends
steps.description: Square the stepped ends on a crosscut sled.
safetyBanners: DANGER: Never use the rip fence as a length stop for crosscuts. Use a crosscut sled with a stop block set before the blade, so the offcut is never trapped between blade and fence.

steps.title: Flatten and sand
steps.description: Flatten with a router sled or drum sander, never the thickness planer. Sand 80, 120, 180 grit. Break edges (180 grit).
safetyBanners: DANGER: Never run an end-grain glue-up through the thickness planer. It can blow apart. Flatten with a router sled or drum sander.

steps.title: Edge profile
steps.description: Rout the edge profile, default: 1/8" (3 mm) roundover. Optional finger grips: core box / round-nose bit 3/8–1/2" (9.5–12.7 mm).
safetyBanners: WARNING: Climb cuts can grab. Feed the router against the bit rotation and take shallow passes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.description: Raise the grain with a damp cloth, sand 180 again, then flood with food-safe mineral oil and top with board butter.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use closed-grain, non-toxic hardwoods only. Avoid spalted, softwood or oily/sensitising exotics on cutting surfaces.

planerTextRule.faceTooWideForJointerText: Too wide for the jointer ({jointerMax}): flatten one face on a planer sled first, then plane the other face parallel

widthRule.text: A panel wider than the planer max width (305 mm) goes to the router sled or drum sander. Face-joint only boards no wider than the jointer max width (152 mm); wider boards get a planer sled or are flattened by hand.

blankRule.panelWidthText: A panel no wider than 12" (305 mm) is planed. A wider panel is either flattened on the router sled or drum sander, or glued as sub-panels of whole strips each no wider than 305 mm, which are planed and then crosscut separately (end-grain boards line the slices up at the end-grain glue-up; do not re-glue a wide panel just to crosscut it). Splits fall only on strip glue lines, never through a strip. Crosscut every slice on a crosscut sled with a stop block, never against the rip fence. Each crosscut step prints the panel width the sled must clear, sheet units first. If that width is over 24" (610 mm), split the panel first; never freehand a panel that wide.
blankRule.text: Mill and rip whole blanks before any crosscut. A blank is a glued strip-set panel: every strip across the board width, glued in pattern order (N strips = squares or strips across), not one strip per species. Panel width = sum of strip widths + width oversize. Slice count = rows along the board length (not total pieces). Blank length = max(305 mm, slices x (slice + kerf) + 2 x 25 mm trim). If that exceeds 915 mm (36"), split the slices across the fewest equal panels that each fit 305-915 mm; never cap a panel and drop slices. Never send a crosscut slice or piece shorter than 305 mm to the jointer or planer.

handHole.text: Hand-hole slot 4" (100 mm) long x 1" (25.4 mm) wide, round ends, centred 1-1/2" (38 mm) in from the end. Rout through with a template and a 1/2" (12.7 mm) bit in shallow passes.

fingerGrip.text: Finger grips 4" (100 mm) long, routed into the end grain of each end with a core box bit, centred on the width.

notes: Take ~1/64" (0.4 mm) passes for final surfacing.
